analysis: The PR changes `.github/workflows/register-model.yml` to add a `publish_revision_only` mode. This mode POSTs `{version, hugging_face_artifact}` to `/v1/admin/models/{urlencoded model_id}/publish-revision`, using `MODEL_REGISTRY_PUBLISHING_KEY` (the same secret as before). Registration-only inputs are now optional in the workflow UI. The registration path adds a shell non-empty check (`${!field}`) and a jq positive-integer check. Inputs are passed through env vars (no direct script injection), and `model_id` is percent-encoded with python `urllib.parse.quote(safe='')`, so path injection is mitigated. The doc and changelog edits mention `scripts/test_model_registry_workflow.py` and `scripts/test_publish_model_revision.py`, which are not in this diff, so the tests are unreviewed. No provider, coordinator wire, attestation, App Attest or encryption code changes, so TB-002, TB-011 and T-052..T-058 are unaffected. The one concern is a supply-chain-adjacent admin action: revision-only always promotes (it ignores the `promote` input), with no environment approval gate and with backend validation of the endpoint out of scope. The backend `publish-revision` semantics are platform-owned and were not visible. For example, a null `hugging_face_artifact` might clear a pinned HF source. A later pass should confirm this against the platform.

findings.detail: In `publish_revision_only` mode, the payload at lines 190-192 contains only `version` and `hugging_face_artifact`. The `promote` input is dropped, and the input description says the mode will 'Publish and promote'. An operator who sets `promote=false` together with `publish_revision_only=true` expecting a staged-only publish therefore sends a request that, per the documentation, promotes the revision. Promotion changes the manifest providers download and verify (A-004, T-027, T-012) and is meant to need specific approval. The workflow has no environment or approval gate; a single publishing key is enough, and the script does not validate that `version` matches a reviewed upload. Fix: reject `promote=false` when `publish_revision_only` is set, or send an explicit promote flag and let the backend honour it. Put the job behind a protected GitHub environment with required reviewers. Also require a non-null pinned `hugging_face_artifact` or document what null does to an existing pinned source.
findings.title: Revision-only mode ignores the `promote` input and always promotes
